// Command smokehost is the FUL-1651 phase-2 smoke harness. It maps the three
// documented cluster env vars onto the landed raft packages and runs the flow
// group, so the smoke observes the real discovery, bootstrap, eviction and
// recovery code paths rather than a reimplementation of them.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/hashicorp/go-hclog"
	"github.com/hashicorp/raft"
	machine "github.com/whitaker-io/machine/v4"
	"github.com/whitaker-io/machine/raft/checkpoint"
	"github.com/whitaker-io/machine/raft/ledger"
	"github.com/whitaker-io/machine/raft/membership"
	"github.com/whitaker-io/machine/raft/recovery"
	"github.com/whitaker-io/machine/raft/transport"
)

// mirrorResolvePeers is a BYTE-FOR-BYTE MIRROR of the landed
// membership.resolvePeers (raft/membership/config.go:32) — same SplitHostPort,
// same net.DefaultResolver.LookupHost, same JoinHostPort, same sort. It exists
// because Manager.resolveLive is unexported and step 4.3's isolation must report
// what the eviction round SAW, not what a differently-written resolver returns.
//
// A MIRROR IS A CLAIM AND IT IS DISCLOSED AS ONE: if the landed resolver ever
// stops agreeing with this copy, this probe reports the wrong live set and the
// isolation it produces is wrong with it. The probe therefore never asserts —
// it only records, beside the group's real committed configuration, which the
// harness reads through the public Manager.Membership.
func mirrorResolvePeers(ctx context.Context, peers string) ([]string, error) {
	host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(peers)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	found, err := net.DefaultResolver.LookupHost(ctx, host)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(found))
	for _, addr := range found {
		out = append(out, net.JoinHostPort(addr, port))
	}
	sort.Strings(out)
	return out, nil
}

func containsAddr(live []string, addr string) bool {
	for _, item := range live {
		if item == addr {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// evictArm names WHICH branch of the landed eviction round this node's current
// state would take, computed from the same inputs the round reads.
//
// WHY THIS IS THE DELIVERABLE OF STEP 4.3 RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. Four of the
// round's exits produce NO LOG LINE AT ALL — not the leader, no absent member,
// bound 4's empty-or-self-missing resolution, and a failed GetConfiguration —
// so an observer watching the logs cannot tell a round that ran and declined
// from a round that never ran. Two more exits log only at Debug. A rolling
// update that leaves dead voters in the configuration with no eviction line is
// therefore consistent with at least four different mechanisms, which is exactly
// why three runs of the same command produced three outcomes and none of them
// named a cause.
//
// THE ARMS, in the order evictRound and evictOne take them:
//   not-leader           evictRound, r.State() != raft.Leader          (silent)
//   resolve-failed       evictRound, resolveLive returned an error     (Warn)
//   no-absent-member     evictOne, absentMember found nothing          (silent)
//   bound4-empty         evictionPermitted, len(live) == 0             (silent)
//   bound4-self-missing  evictionPermitted, live lacks this advertise  (silent)
//   bound1-incomplete    evictionPermitted, len(live) < Expect         (Debug)
//   bound2-below-live    evictionPermitted, voters-cost < len(live)    (Debug)
//   would-evict          all bounds pass; RemoveServer would be called (Warn)
func evictArm(servers []raft.Server, live []string, advertise string, expect int) (string, string) {
	victim := ""
	suffrage := ""
	found := false
	for _, s := range servers {
		if !containsAddr(live, string(s.Address)) {
			victim = string(s.ID)
			suffrage = s.Suffrage.String()
			found = true
			break
		}
	}
	if !found {
		return "no-absent-member", ""
	}
	if len(live) == 0 {
		return "bound4-empty", victim
	}
	if !containsAddr(live, advertise) {
		return "bound4-self-missing", victim
	}
	if expect > 0 && len(live) < expect {
		return "bound1-incomplete", victim
	}
	voters := 0
	for _, s := range servers {
		if s.Suffrage == raft.Voter {
			voters++
		}
	}
	cost := 0
	if suffrage == raft.Voter.String() {
		cost = 1
	}
	if voters-cost < len(live) {
		return "bound2-below-live", victim
	}
	return "would-evict", victim
}

func main() {
	logger := hclog.New(&hclog.LoggerOptions{
		Name: "smokehost", Level: hclog.Debug, Output: os.Stdout,
	})

	node := os.Getenv("MACHINE_NODE_ID")
	advertise := os.Getenv("MACHINE_ADVERTISE")
	bind := os.Getenv("MACHINE_BIND")
	flow := os.Getenv("MACHINE_FLOW")
	peers := os.Getenv("MACHINE_CLUSTER_PEERS")
	secret := os.Getenv("MACHINE_CLUSTER_SECRET")
	// LEDGER_ID exists ONLY to drive the diverged-identity shape: when it is set
	// and differs from MACHINE_NODE_ID, the ledger reports one id and
	// membership.Config.Node carries another, which is the disagreement
	// ErrIdentityDiverged refuses.
	ledgerID := os.Getenv("MACHINE_LEDGER_ID")
	if ledgerID == "" {
		ledgerID = node
	}
	expect := 0
	if v := os.Getenv("MACHINE_CLUSTER_EXPECT"); v != "" {
		n, err := strconv.Atoi(v)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "smokehost: MACHINE_CLUSTER_EXPECT:", err)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		expect = n
	}

	addr, err := net.ResolveTCPAddr("tcp", advertise)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "smokehost: advertise:", err)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	mux, err := transport.New(transport.Config{
		BindAddr:  bind,
		Advertise: addr,
		Logger:    logger.Named("mux"),
		Tokens:    []transport.Token{transport.Token(secret)},
	})
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "smokehost: mux:", err)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	defer mux.Close()

	manager, err := membership.New(membership.Config{
		Node:      node,
		Advertise: advertise,
		Mux:       mux,
		Logger:    logger.Named("membership"),
		Flows:     []string{flow},
		Peers:     peers,
		Expect:    expect,
		Open: func(f string) (*ledger.Ledger, error) {
			return ledger.Open(ledger.Config{
				Flow: f, LocalID: ledgerID, Mux: mux, Logger: logger.Named("ledger"),
			})
		},
	})
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "smokehost: membership.New:", err)
		os.Exit(2)
	}

	// THE PROMOTER CANNOT SEE A JOINER CATCH UP WITHOUT THIS. Every node answers
	// for itself over the control channel, and flowPilot.FetchServerStats reads
	// exactly this callback; a host that omits it leaves every staged nonvoter
	// permanently unpromoted, which reads as a promotion defect and is not one.
	//
	// MACHINE_DISABLE_LOCAL_STATS EXISTS ONLY TO DRIVE THAT SHAPE DELIBERATELY.
	// The smoke's fail-silent leg needs a fleet that omits the callback so it can
	// record what the promoter says, if anything, when its stats are absent.
	if os.Getenv("MACHINE_DISABLE_LOCAL_STATS") != "" {
		logger.Warn("SMOKEHOST-NO-LOCAL-STATS", "node", node,
			"note", "the local stats callback is deliberately not installed")
	} else {
		manager.SetLocalStats(func(f string) (membership.FlowStats, bool) {
			l, ok := manager.Ledger(f)
			if !ok {
				return membership.FlowStats{}, false
			}
			r := l.Raft()
			st := r.Stats()
			parse := func(k string) uint64 {
				n, _ := strconv.ParseUint(st[k], 10, 64)
				return n
			}
			lc := time.Duration(0)
			if d, err := time.ParseDuration(st["last_contact"]); err == nil {
				lc = d
			}
			return membership.FlowStats{
				Term:        parse("term"),
				LastIndex:   parse("last_log_index"),
				LastContact: lc,
				Voter:       st["state"] != "",
				Leader:      r.State() == 2,
			}, true
		})
	}

	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()

	if err := manager.Start(ctx); err != nil {
		// THE REFUSAL IS PRINTED VERBATIM AND THE PROCESS EXITS NON-ZERO. The
		// diverged-identity leg reads this line.
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "smokehost: start:", err)
		os.Exit(3)
	}
	defer manager.Close()

	logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-UP", "node", node, "flow", flow, "advertise", advertise, "expect", expect)

	// STEP 4.4 ONLY. Nothing but the recovery observation sets MACHINE_FLOW_RUN,
	// so every other phase-4 step runs the harness exactly as steps 4.1 through
	// 4.3 observed it.
	if os.Getenv("MACHINE_FLOW_RUN") != "" {
		runRecoveryFlow(ctx, logger, manager, flow, node)
	}

	tick := time.NewTicker(2 * time.Second)
	defer tick.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return
		case <-tick.C:
			cfg, _, ok := manager.Membership(flow)
			if !ok {
				logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-STATE", "node", node, "flow", flow, "members", "none")
				continue
			}
			out := ""
			for _, s := range cfg.Servers {
				out += fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s ", s.ID, s.Suffrage)
			}
			logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-STATE", "node", node, "flow", flow, "members", out)

			// STEP 4.3'S ISOLATION PROBE. It reports which branch of the landed
			// eviction round this node's state would take, on the LEADER only,
			// because the round itself returns on a non-leader before logging
			// anything. Four of the round's exits are silent, so without this a
			// rolling update that leaves dead voters behind is consistent with
			// several different mechanisms and names none of them.
			//
			// IT OBSERVES AND NEVER ACTS. Nothing here calls RemoveServer or
			// mutates membership; the landed code remains the only thing that
			// evicts. The line is prefixed SMOKEHOST- so the fail-silent leg's
			// recorder excludes it with the rest of the harness's own output.
			l, ok := manager.Ledger(flow)
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			state := l.Raft().State().String()
			if l.Raft().State() != raft.Leader {
				logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-EVICTPROBE", "node", node, "flow", flow,
					"state", state, "arm", "not-leader")
				continue
			}
			live, err := mirrorResolvePeers(ctx, peers)
			if err != nil {
				logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-EVICTPROBE", "node", node, "flow", flow,
					"state", state, "arm", "resolve-failed", "error", err)
				continue
			}
			arm, victim := evictArm(cfg.Servers, live, advertise, expect)
			logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-EVICTPROBE", "node", node, "flow", flow,
				"state", state, "arm", arm, "victim", victim,
				"resolved", len(live), "expect", expect,
				"self_in_resolution", containsAddr(live, advertise),
				"live", fmt.Sprintf("%v", live), "members", out)
		}
	}
}

// runRecoveryFlow builds a Machine whose journal IS the landed recovery detector,
// wires the flow flowc generated from recover.flow, and serves the small control
// surface the recovery recorder drives.
//
// WHY THE HARNESS RUNS THE FLOW AT ALL. Carry-in (e) is about a CHECKPOINTED FLOW
// surviving a real pod deletion. Every recovery leg in lane E is verified against
// real multi-node raft groups, but always with the worker killed as a goroutine. A
// killed pod differs: the process, its memory, its transport connections and its
// raft node all go at once, and the leader learns of it through membership rather
// than through a closed channel. Nothing short of running the real flow in the real
// pod exercises that.
//
// THE JOURNAL IS THE REAL ONE. recovery.New(ledger, manager, flow) returns the
// landed Detector, which satisfies machine.Journal with Checkpoint, Claim, Retire
// and Orphans, and the machine's own resume loop consumes Orphans per checkpointed
// worker. The harness adds no recovery logic of its own and could not: the point is
// to observe the landed code, not to reimplement it.
func runRecoveryFlow(ctx context.Context, logger hclog.Logger, manager *membership.Manager, flow, node string) {
	l, ok := manager.Ledger(flow)
	if !ok {
		logger.Error("SMOKEHOST-FLOW-NOJOURNAL", "flow", flow)
		return
	}
	det := recovery.New(l, manager, flow)
	m := machine.New("smokehost-"+flow, machine.OptionJournal(det))
	ingests, err := WireRecover(m)
	if err != nil {
		logger.Error("SMOKEHOST-FLOW-WIRE-FAILED", "flow", flow, "error", err)
		return
	}
	if err := m.Start(ctx); err != nil {
		logger.Error("SMOKEHOST-FLOW-START-FAILED", "flow", flow, "error", err)
		return
	}
	logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-FLOW-UP", "node", node, "flow", flow, "localid", det.LocalID())

	mux := http.NewServeMux()

	// /hold makes THIS pod park the next datum its checkpointed node receives, so
	// a checkpoint record exists with a live owner when the pod is deleted.
	mux.HandleFunc("/hold", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		gate.Set()
		logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-FLOW-HOLD", "node", node)
		fmt.Fprintln(w, "holding")
	})

	// /release unblocks whatever this pod is parking.
	mux.HandleFunc("/release", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		gate.Release()
		logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-FLOW-RELEASE", "node", node)
		fmt.Fprintln(w, "released")
	})

	// /ingest pushes one datum through the GENERATED package's exported typed
	// ingest — the same surface step 3.1 observed, here on a real pod.
	mux.HandleFunc("/ingest", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		id := r.URL.Query().Get("id")
		if id == "" {
			http.Error(w, "id is required", http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		if err := ingests.Ingest(r.Context(), Job{ID: id}); err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
			return
		}
		logger.Info("SMOKEHOST-FLOW-INGEST", "node", node, "id", id)
		fmt.Fprintln(w, "ingested", id)
	})

	// /recovery reports, for every checkpoint the flow's journal holds, who the
	// record says owns it and WHO THE LEDGER SAYS HOLDS THE CLAIM.
	//
	// THE CLAIMANT IS READ THROUGH Ledger.Claimant AND NEVER FROM ANYTHING THE
	// RECORDER WROTE. That accessor is the only way to observe claim state at all:
	// claims are kept apart from journaled values so Get's reply stays a truthful
	// set entry, which means a held claim is INVISIBLE through Get. The key is the
	// CLAIM PATH rather than the bare datum, because the fsm keys its claim map by
	// the appended entry's Path and the detector appends at checkpoint.ClaimPath.
	mux.HandleFunc("/recovery", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		entries, err := l.List(r.Context(), "checkpoint/")
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
			return
		}
		type row struct {
			Datum    string `json:"datum"`
			Claimant string `json:"claimant"`
			Held     bool   `json:"held"`
		}
		out := make([]row, 0, len(entries))
		for _, e := range entries {
			datum := strings.TrimPrefix(e.Path, "checkpoint/")
			owner, held, err := l.Claimant(r.Context(), checkpoint.ClaimPath(datum))
			if err != nil {
				http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
				return
			}
			out = append(out, row{Datum: datum, Claimant: owner, Held: held})
		}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(out)
	})

	// /health lets the recorder pick the leader without parsing logs.
	mux.HandleFunc("/health", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		state := "unknown"
		if lg, ok := manager.Ledger(flow); ok {
			state = lg.Raft().State().String()
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(w, "node=%s state=%s holding=%t\n", node, state, gate.Held())
	})

	srv := &http.Server{Addr: ":8080", Handler: mux}
	go func() {
		<-ctx.Done()
		_ = srv.Close()
	}()
	go func() {
		if err := srv.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
			logger.Error("SMOKEHOST-FLOW-HTTP-FAILED", "error", err)
		}
	}()
}
